newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia non-residential building to grow.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia non-residential building to grow.

text.p: Australia's non-residential building industry activity is expected to grow nine percent in 1996/97 in its fourth consecutive year of growth, economic consultant BIS Shrapnel said on Monday.
"Growth will be fuelled by double digit increases in office, hotel, and social and institutional building commencements," director of building services Robert Mellor said in a statement.
But he said other sectors would remain weak.
Non-residential building rose 10 percent in 1995/96 due to substantial increases in the commercial and industrial sectors.
Mellor said office building commencements were expected to rise 27 percent in 1996/97, largely as a result of accelerated activity in the states of New South Wales and Queensland.
He said retail building was expected to grow only one percent because of oversupply resulting from a high level of extensions and refurbishments to shopping centres.
"As a result, fewer investment funds will flow into the sector because returns will not be so high as in the recent past," he said.
Hotel building was forecast to rise 16 percent in 1996/97, while factory commencements were expected to fall seven percent.
"This forecast is based on the manufacturing sector holding back on capacity expansion because of weak domestic growth in sales," Mellor said.
